anomalies.observed: On the CAN BUS sheet, the MCP2515 SPI slave data pins are wired with the net CAN_CIPO on the SI (slave-in / MOSI) pin and CAN_COPI on the SO (slave-out / MISO) pin (page 6 U8 pin14=CAN_CIPO, pin15=CAN_COPI; page 10 U9 pin14=CAN_CIPO, pin15=CAN_COPI).
anomalies.expected: COPI (Controller Out / Peripheral In) is the master->slave data line and must connect to the slave's SI; CIPO (Controller In / Peripheral Out) is the slave->master line and must connect to the slave's SO. The board's own SPI Naming Note states 'COPI Controller Out, Peripheral In / CIPO Controller In, Peripheral Out', and the SC16IS752 UART expanders on the same SPI family are wired correctly (U13 pin11 SI=SERIAL_COPI, pin12 SO=SERIAL_CIPO). The CAN controllers therefore have MOSI and MISO swapped.

evidence.quote: CAN BUS sheet (page 6): U8 MCP2515-xSO, pin14 net label 'CAN_CIPO', pin15 net label 'CAN_COPI'
CAN BUS sheet (page 10): U9 MCP2515-xSO, pin14 'CAN_CIPO', pin15 'CAN_COPI'
Serial sheet (page 8): U13 SC16IS752, pin11 A1/SI = SERIAL_COPI, pin12 SD = SERIAL_CIPO (correct reference)
SPI Naming Note: COPI 'Controller Out, Peripheral In' CIPO 'Controller In, Peripheral Out'

anomalies.impact: The SPI bus to both CAN controllers is reversed: the controller's serial-out drives the master's serial-out and vice-versa. The MCP2515s cannot be configured or polled, so CAN0 and CAN1 never come up and the rover cannot communicate with the Odrive motor controllers over the isolated CAN buses.

parsed.summary: The board matches the specification in its headline items (16 MHz crystals on Y1/Y2, LTC4412 ideal-diode U6, SN74LVC1G07 e-stop buffers, ISL54222AIUZ analog switch, WS2812 chain), but the SPI data lines to the two MCP2515 CAN controllers (U8/U9) appear swapped relative to the correctly-wired UART expanders, which would break CAN0/CAN1.
